tagline: One role, many users — filter rows using the logged-in user's identity

slides.title: Dynamic Row-Level Security
slides.body: Dynamic RLS uses the current user's email (from USERPRINCIPALNAME()) at report load time to filter data automatically. One role definition serves all users — each sees only their authorized rows.
slides.keyPoint: Define one role with a DAX filter using USERPRINCIPALNAME(). Assign all regional managers to that same role — the DAX handles the per-user filtering.

slides.title: Security Mapping Table — SalesAccess
slides.caption: A separate table maps user emails to their authorized region
slides.note: This table is imported into the model. It has NO relationship to other tables — LOOKUPVALUE handles the lookup without one.

slides.title: RLS DAX Filter on DimRegion
slides.code:
-- Role: 'RegionManager'
-- Filter expression applied to DimRegion table:

[Region] = LOOKUPVALUE(
    SalesAccess[AllowedRegion],
    SalesAccess[ManagerEmail],
    USERPRINCIPALNAME()
)
slides.annotation: USERPRINCIPALNAME() returns the email of the user viewing the report in Power BI Service. LOOKUPVALUE finds their authorized region and restricts DimRegion to that value.

slides.title: Alice Views the Report
slides.note: alice@corp.com → AllowedRegion = 'North' → DimRegion filtered to North → FactSales restricted to North rows via relationship

slides.title: Critical Security Trap — LOOKUPVALUE Blank Vulnerability
bullets: When LOOKUPVALUE finds no matching email, it returns BLANK
[Region] = BLANK() evaluates to TRUE for rows where Region is null or empty
This means users NOT in the SalesAccess table see all rows with null Region — a data leak!
slides.warning: The LOOKUPVALUE BLANK vulnerability is a top PL-300 exam trap. The 'intermittent data leakage' symptom (some managers see too much data, others don't) is the classic tell.

slides.title: Roles vs Users — How Assignment Works
bullets: You define one role ('RegionManager') with the LOOKUPVALUE DAX filter
In Power BI Service → Security settings, you assign Azure AD users or groups to that role
Executives who need all data: assign to a separate role with NO filter (unfiltered role = sees everything)
When a user belongs to multiple roles, Power BI applies the UNION — most permissive wins
slides.keyPoint: If an executive is assigned to both 'RegionManager' and an unfiltered 'Executive' role, they see ALL data — the unfiltered role takes precedence via union semantics.
